name: Experimental Methods in Physics
description: Introduction to experimental physics: purpose, reproducibility, error types (random/systematic), precision versus accuracy, probability distributions, error propagation. Transport measurements: four-probe method, Hall effect, contact resistance, R–T dependence, scattering mechanisms. Optical and structural techniques: photoluminescence (bandgap, excitons), XRD (Bragg’s law, peak indexing), Raman spectroscopy (vibrational modes, strain analysis), XPS (core-level spectroscopy). Microscopy: STM (LDOS, dI/dV), SEM (electron-beam interaction). Soft matter systems: viscoelasticity, optical tweezers, microrheology. Astronomy: multi-messenger observations, dark matter, gravitational lensing. Includes data acquisition, lock-in amplifiers, spectral calibration, microscopy image analysis, python/MATLAB-based model fitting, and interpretation of real-world experimental data.
